title: Avalon Retail — POC cost & benchmark scoping
next_steps: Send detailed per-token cost spreadsheet with multiple batching scenarios
Share SOC2 + private deployment security pack
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run next week and invite Avalon infra team
Follow up with pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted with 6-month runway options
action_items: Jordan: send cost model spreadsheet and raw benchmark templates by 2026-08-21
Priya: prepare suggested batching/cache config and expected latency bounds by 2026-08-24
Marcus: provision test VPC and add Redwood IPs by 2026-08-22

header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-19 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Marcus Ng (Avalon Head of Platform), Sofia Alvarez (Avalon ML), Derek Li (Avalon CTO), Hannah Price (Avalon Product)
summary: POC scoping focused on unit economics: per-token estimates, batching and caching knobs, benchmark plan and timeline. Avalon has strict budget limits, needs <= $0.0008 per generated token for the primary use case and requires private VPC option and SOC2 evidence. Agreed next: Redwood to send cost model spreadsheet, Avalon to provision test VPC, schedule 2-hour benchmark next week.
topics: Per-token cost assumptions and batching knobs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. This is Jordan from Redwood. Uh yeah we wanted to go through the POC scope, specifically the cost model and bench plan.
[00:12] Marcus: Thanks, Jordan. Quick intro — Marcus, head of platform at Avalon. We have Sofia on ML and Derek's on for any infra stuff. Our key ask up front: we have a hard budget constraint and we need to show per token costs to finance.
[00:26] Jordan: Totally, that's main objective. Can you share target numbers? like monthly tokens, p95 latency goals, and what you consider success?
[00:34] Sofia: For the shopping assistant flow, average prompt is about 120 tokens in, expect ~220 tokens out. Peak QPS is low, maybe 6 to 8 requests per second, but we need p95 latency under 350 ms for the quick-reply experience. Budget wise finance told us target is around 80 cents per thousand generated tokens so roughly $0.0008 per token.
[00:56] Priya: Ok that budget is tight but not impossible. Important to clarify: is that across both input+output tokens or only generated tokens? Cuz caching/prefix reuse can reduce billable tokens in many flows.
[01:10] Sofia: Mostly generated tokens, that's what the product team cares about. We can consider reuse for repeated prompts though, like saved cart templates.
[01:18] Derek: Also we need to know if Hosted plan can meet our security posture. We are leaning toward Redwood Private (VPC) if the economics still work.
[01:26] Jordan: Understood. We'll model both Hosted (fast start) and Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we assume multi-tenant hardware with shared KV cache; for Private we'll show reserved GPU pricing plus expected utilization.
[01:38] Liam: Quick note on quantization — if your model type can be int8 or 4-bit, the per-token compute cost changes a lot. We'll include model variants in the spreadsheet.
[01:47] Marcus: Great. On benchmarks — we want a 2 hour continuous run with representative traffic, and a shorter 15 minute cold-start test. Can Redwood execute from our VPC or do we need to egress?
[01:58] Priya: We can run the benchmark inside your VPC if you provide network peering and Redwood's test runners. For Dedicated we'd run on your tenancy or on reserved infra in our Dedicated pool, either's possible. There may be some initial handshake for KMS keys if you require CMK.
[02:12] Hannah: For timelines, we need results within two weeks, otherwise leadership will push the project later. 2-week turnaround is key.
[02:20] Jordan: Two weeks is tight but doable if bench prep starts today. Next: success criteria — is it strictly cost + latency, or also correctness / hallucination thresholds?
[02:30] Sofia: Both. Cost + p95 latency are gating, but we also need accuracy clerical for entity extraction — F1 at least 0.92 on our eval set. We'll provide eval prompts.
[02:42] Derek: Also, if Dedicated shows much better per-token cost at scale, we'll consider a 6 month commit. So the cost model should show breakpoint where Dedicated becomes cheaper.
[02:53] Priya: We'll include a breakeven analysis: per-token cost vs utilization curve. We'll show batching impact: e.g., single-request beam vs 8–16 token batching and how latency shifts.
[03:05] Marcus: Can you give a ballpark now? Even rough numbers help our finance.
[03:08] Jordan: Rough rough — hosted on a mid-sized open model might be around $0.0012 per generated token with conservative batching; with aggressive batching and prefix caching that can drop to ~$0.0006. Dedicated reserved capacity with good utilization might be in the $0.00035–$0.00065 range depending on quantization. So your $0.0008 target is in the zone but depends on caching and batch windows.
[03:33] Sofia: That range is helpful. But 350ms p95 — will batching break that?
[03:38] Priya: Right, batching trades latency for cost. We can do micro-batching (20–40 ms accumulation windows) which has minimal latency impact at low QPS; for your QPS of 6–8 we can set continuous batching with a 1-request fast path to prioritize latency. Also prefix/KV cache will lower compute when repeated contexts show up.
[03:57] Marcus: What about tokenization overhead and 95th percentile token length? Adaptive batching can blow up tokens, or am I misunderstanding?
[04:05] Priya: Tokenization just increases counts; we need your 95th percentile input length to estimate worst-case. We asked for those in the action items.
[04:13] Hannah: On security, SOC2 is a must, and we need KMS for key control plus audit logs for every request. Are those included?
[04:21] Jordan: Redwood has SOC2 Type II — we'll send the package. KMS integration is available for Private, and we can surface per-request audit logs in the Console. For Hosted, we have encryption at rest but if you need CMK we recommend Private.
[04:37] Derek: Network egress and data residency — our EU customers must keep logs in EU region. Can Redwood pin region?
[04:44] Priya: Yes we can pin model serving to regions and for Private we'd deploy into your VPC region. Hosted also has region selection but with some constraints for capacity. We'll note that in the plan.
[04:55] Marcus: For the bench itself, what metrics will Redwood produce? We need per-token cost, latency percentiles, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.
[05:03] Liam: We'll produce a bench artifact: token-level accounting CSV, latency p50/p95/p99, GPU util over time, batching buckets, and a breakdown of cost components (compute, memory, infra, licensing if applicable).
[05:15] Sofia: Will you include the effect of quantization? Our model might do 4-bit with some quality hit. We need to see delta in F1 vs latency/cost.
[05:23] Priya: Yep. We'll run variants — FP16 baseline, int8, and 4-bit if available — and we'll run your eval set to check quality regression. We'll tag the runs so you can compare cost vs F1.
[05:33] Marcus: About billing — do you bill per-token only or are there capacity charges during Dedicated POC?
[05:40] Jordan: For POC we can do a blended model: usage plus a small reserved test capacity fee for Dedicated. We'll flag it clearly. Our model spreadsheet will show per-token unit cost for hosted scenarios and amortized cost for Dedicated across utilization levels.
[05:53] Hannah: Can we include a scenario where we batch within the client? like client-side bundling to reduce per-token overhead?
[05:58] Priya: Client-side bundling helps for many workflows. We'll add that as a scenario in the spreadsheet. It typically helps when requests are small and you can combine multiple into one call within latency constraints.
[06:10] Sofia: One other thing — we have a heavy reranking job that will be backend-only and latency tolerant, that might be a good candidate for Dedicated because it can use larger batch sizes and more tokens.
[06:20] Liam: Exactly — reranking is perfect for throughput-oriented Dedicated capacity, and it will show much lower per-token costs when you amortize GPU across large batches.
[06:29] Marcus: Ok, for the POC acceptance we propose: per-token cost <= $0.0008 OR Dedicated breakeven within 3 months of expected traffic; p95 latency <= 350ms for the interactive flow; F1 >= 0.92 on evals; and security checks passed.
[06:46] Jordan: That sounds like sensible acceptance criteria. We'll draft a short success criteria doc and attach to the spreadsheet.
[06:53] Derek: How will throttling or fallbacks work in peak? We need graceful degradation.
[06:58] Priya: Redwood has routing policies: fall back to a smaller model or lower-cost region, and circuit-breakers. We'll demo a canary and fallback during the bench run so you can see failover behavior.
[07:10] Hannah: I want to see cost runbooks — operational playbooks for when costs spike.
[07:15] Jordan: We'll include a draft runbook: triggers on token cost delta, auto-scaling suggestions, and immediate mitigations (lower temperature, reduce response length, enable cache).
[07:26] Marcus: Ok can you confirm the exact deliverables and dates?
[07:30] Jordan: Deliverables: 1) Cost model spreadsheet with Hosted vs Dedicated scenarios and batching/caching knobs (Jordan) — by 2026-08-21. 2) Benchmark plan and runner scripts (Priya) — by 2026-08-22. 3) Security package (SOC2, KMS notes) — by 2026-08-21. 4) 2-hour benchmark run scheduled for 2026-08-25 (tentative) with results within 48 hours.
[07:52] Marcus: That timeline is okay. We'll aim to have VPC ready by 2026-08-22.
[07:57] Sofia: We'll also upload the eval set and sample prompts to the shared drive.
[08:01] Jordan: Perfect. Any final questions?
[08:05] Derek: For the Dedicated price, do you offer trial credits for the POC?
[08:09] Jordan: We can offer a trial discount on the reserved test capacity — we'll propose two options in the spreadsheet: short trial credit vs reduced rate for first 3 months.
[08:18] Marcus: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:20] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and schedule.
[08:24] [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard words, speaker overlaps, and some product names transcribed inconsistently (e.g., KV cache as K-V dash cache).
